title: Too Many Alerts
question: Which alert deserves the first scoped investigation when severity and business impact disagree?
briefing: A lab workstation has twelve high-severity signature alerts. A billing-service session has one medium-severity access alert. Neither alert establishes who acted. Your authority is to acquire records and recommend a session-scoped response through Billing Operations. You cannot approve your own control or disable an entire account or service.
lesson: Priority is the order of useful work based on consequence and evidence; severity is a source label.

queries.label: Establish the task and business consequence
queries.question: What is this service for, and which consequences change investigation priority?
queries.can: Names the normal task, related scopes, owners and interruption consequence.
queries.cannot: Does not establish who performed the current action.

queries.label: Check the exact work authorisation
queries.question: Does approved work cover this session, task, target and period?
queries.cannot: Does not prove the human operator or the activity that actually occurred.

queries.label: Inspect the scoped session activity
queries.question: Which action was recorded for this named session within collection limits?
queries.can: Records session-level actions and the observed target.

queries.label: Check the service transaction independently
queries.question: Does the service-side transaction establish the same scoped operation?
queries.can: Tests the operation through a separately collected service transaction.
queries.cannot: A second card alone does not establish a sufficient explanation.

facts.title: Starting observations
facts.text: A lab workstation has twelve high-severity signature alerts. A billing-service session has one medium-severity access alert. Neither alert establishes who acted.

facts.title: Task, scope and business consequence
facts.text: The lab is a scheduled isolated test environment. The billing service handles live invoice approvals and has no equivalent overnight redundancy. Business consequence supports reviewing the billing session first, regardless of alert count.

facts.title: The specific work authorisation
facts.text: The approved settlement test names the billing session, its service identity, the read-only invoice sample and the current review period.

facts.title: Recorded session activity
facts.text: The billing session read the exact invoice sample listed in the approved settlement test; no payment destination change appears in the covered session interval.

facts.title: An independently collected transaction
facts.text: The invoice service independently recorded the matching read-only sample transaction and no payment-destination write for this named session.

facts.title: Verified business-context response
facts.text: A pre-established directory contact confirmed the task record: The approved settlement test names the billing session, its service identity, the read-only invoice sample and the current review period. This confirms the business record, not the person operating the session.

facts.title: The specific work authorisation
facts.text: The approved settlement test permits read-only invoice checks. It does not authorise changing payment destinations or using this interactive billing session.

facts.title: Recorded session activity
facts.text: The billing session submitted a payment-destination change outside the read-only settlement test. This source records that session action, not the person operating it.

facts.title: An independently collected transaction
facts.text: The payment workflow independently recorded a destination-change request from the billing session, outside the disclosed read-only job.

facts.title: Verified business-context response
facts.text: A pre-established directory contact confirmed the task record: The approved settlement test permits read-only invoice checks. It does not authorise changing payment destinations or using this interactive billing session. This confirms the business record, not the person operating the session.

facts.title: Work record unavailable
facts.text: The work-authorisation archive is unavailable for the named session and period. No approval or denial can be inferred.

facts.title: Session collection unavailable
facts.text: The session-audit source did not collect the relevant historical interval. Absence of a record cannot establish the absence of activity.

facts.title: Independent collection is limited
facts.text: The independent service journal lacks the target application operation for the historical interval. A different source name does not restore that capability.

facts.title: Verified check timed out
facts.text: The pre-established directory contact did not respond by the stated due step. This is a delivered limitation, not approval or a reason to wait indefinitely.

facts.title: A later scoped transaction
facts.text: The named session performed a further source-recorded operation within the specifically approved task. This later event does not identify the person, establish motive or change any earlier snapshot.

reviewWindow: The named session from its start through the explicit cutoff of each acquired snapshot. A simulation step is an investigation opportunity, not a minute.
